memo: Member is a 24-year-old community-college student enrolled more than half-time in 4 courses. Screening confirms: (1) 88 monthly hours from education activity exceeds the 80-hour standard; (2) documents on hand (enrollment letter and class schedule) satisfy the proof requirement for school; (3) 29 days remain to respond (due 2026-08-15). No exemption applies, but the hours path is clear and fully supported. The member's concern that school 'doesn't count like a job' is unfounded—education at half-time or more is an explicitly named qualifying activity and the standard acceptance proof is exactly what they hold.
member_impact: Good news: your school counts! You're taking 4 classes (more than half-time) with about 88 hours a month of class and homework. That's above the 80 hours you need to show. You already have the two papers that prove it: your enrollment letter and class schedule. Send both to the state by August 15, 2026. You have plenty of time—almost a month. School absolutely counts like a job for Medicaid; the rules say so right there.
recommended_actions: Gather enrollment letter and class schedule (already on hand).
Prepare a cover letter or form listing the documents and stating monthly hours (88).
Submit both documents to the state by 2026-08-15 (29 days remain).

citations.quote: Qualifying activities include working for pay (including self-employment), attending school or an education program at least half-time, participating in a job-training or workforce program, and performing community service or volunteering with a qualifying organization.
An enrollment letter or class schedule proves education hours; half-time enrollment or more satisfies the standard by itself in most months.

findings.detail: Qualifying hours: 88 per month (88h education) — meets the 80-hour standard.
Every claimed activity (1) has an accepted document on hand.
